newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wins usually Republican Florida-tv networks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wins usually Republican Florida-tv networks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton won Florida in the U.S. election, the first time a Democratic candidate has carried the state in 20 years, according to projections by CNN and CBS television on Tuesday.
The last Democratic presidential candidate to win Florida, which has 25 electoral college votes, was Jimmy Carter, who beat then-president Gerald Ford in the state in 1976.
CBS and NBC television also projected that Clinton would win the small New England states of Vermont and New Hampshire.
Vermont, a traditionally liberal-leaning state, has only three electoral college votes. A candidate needs 270 college votes to win the presidency.

New Hampshire has historically been a Republican stronghold. Although the state has only four votes in the electoral college, its loss would be a symbolic blow to Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole.
